author: TradingCalc
description: 100 deterministic tools across options, forex, quant risk/stats, prediction markets, on-chain safety, and crypto futures: Deribit BTC/ETH options (options_payoff, black_scholes, black_scholes_live, straddle_strangle, covered_call_protective_put, implied_volatility), forex (pip value, margin level, breakeven, pnl, risk/reward, scenario, average entry, position size, margin required, currency converter, swap/rollover cost, correlation - manual + live-FX-rate variants), risk/stats (var_cvar, sharpe_stats, hurst_exponent, cointegration, portfolio_tearsheet, garch, risk_parity, dsr, kelly_frontier, unsmoothing, evt_tail_risk, orderbook_impact), prediction markets across Kalshi, Polymarket, Limitless, Myriad and ADI Predictstreet's crypto categories (odds_converter, market_implied_odds, prediction_market_edge, window_fair_value, spread_reader), chain-agnostic on-chain (token_risk_check, swap_price_impact, bonding_curve on Solana; market_cap_comparison and wallet_flag_check on Solana + 5 EVM chains), trade planning (pnl, breakeven, exit_target, scenario, dca_entry, scale_out), risk (liquidation, position_sizing, max_leverage, risk_reward), funding & carry (funding_cost, funding_arb, compound_funding, funding_breakeven, carry_trade), market structure (open_analysis, session_structure, value_migration, breakout_acceptance), crypto spot (crypto_profit), cross-exchange price agreement (price_consensus), primitives (average_entry, hedge_ratio), and integrated decision (pre_trade_check, portfolio_risk). Formulas normalized across 17 exchanges, linear and inverse contracts. Every response signed with ECDSA P-256. Not AI estimates, exact numbers your trading bot can trust.

tools.name: workflow.run_pnl_planning
tools.title: PnL Planning
tools.description: Calculate net PnL, ROE, fees and gross profit/loss for a futures trade. Edge cases: entryPrice, exitPrice and size above zero; feeOpenPct and feeClosePct optional fractions from 0 to 0.05 (0.0002 is 0.02%). For inverse contracts size is USD contracts and results are in the base coin. Not covered: funding payments, slippage, liquidation before the exit price is reached, and taxes. Use when user asks "what's my profit/loss on this trade?" Returns: grossPnl, fees, netPnl, netPnlUsdt, roe (%), maxLossBound (only non-null for an inverse/coin-margined short: the finite ceiling on net coin-denominated loss as price rises without limit, (size/entryPrice)×(1+feeOpenPct) - includes the opening fee, since it survives the exit-price-to-infinity limit while the closing fee vanishes - null for every other side/contractType combination, which either has no such bound or a trivial one).

size.description: Position size: base asset qty for linear, USD contracts for inverse

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, pnl/fees are returned in the base coin, not USDT.

tools.name: workflow.run_liquidation_safety
tools.title: Liquidation Safety
tools.description: Calculate the liquidation price for an isolated-margin futures position with one flat maintenance margin rate (mmr, which you supply from your exchange's tier), unless you use the tiered mode described below. The default is isolated: it does not model a cross account. To get a cross-account figure pass walletBalance, otherMaintenanceMargin and otherUnrealizedPnl (any of them switches to cross, with size required), plus tiers for tiered maintenance margin; there is no separate marginMode parameter. The flat model is generic, for linear and inverse alike, not any one exchange's engine. By default the maintenance margin is taken on the position value at the liquidation price (the form Bybit, KuCoin and Hyperliquid document); mmBase "entry" takes it on the entry value (the form MEXC documents); liqFeeRate adds a liquidation fee to the rate (KuCoin). Optional tiered mode, for tiered maintenance margin and shared (cross) collateral after the Binance USD-M help page (linear) and the Bybit inverse and Binance COIN-M definitions (inverse, size in USD contracts, tier bands, cum, wallet and other-position fields all in the base coin): pass size (required there) and tiers (upTo, mmr, optional cum), optionally walletBalance, otherMaintenanceMargin, otherUnrealizedPnl. In that mode mmr is used only when tiers are left out, mmBase "entry" and liqFeeRate are refused, the last tier is open-ended, and the tier used is the one that holds the notional at the liquidation price (our choice, exchanges do not publish theirs); tier rows are supplied by you, never fetched here (for the current tiers of an exchange by symbol use workflow.run_liquidation_live), and the result then also carries tier {index, mmr, cum}. Without those fields it is the flat model: no tiers and no shared collateral, so it can differ from an exchange's own figure. Edge cases: entryPrice and leverage above zero; mmr 0 to 0.2 (default 0.005); liqFeeRate 0 to 0.05 (default 0, refused in tiered mode); tiered mode needs size, 1 to 50 tiers ascending by upTo, mmr 0 to 0.5 never lower than the previous tier, only the last tier may leave out upTo, and a cum that disagrees with the tier rates is an error; walletBalance above zero, otherOpenMaintenanceMargin 0 or more. Not covered: auto-deleveraging, partial liquidation, mark price versus last price, funding paid while open, and the exchange own engine, which may differ. Use when user asks "where will I get liquidated?" or "how close is my liq price?". Returns: liqPrice (the price). liqPrice is null when the position cannot be liquidated: an inverse short whose margin covers any price rise (at 1x or less with the default mmBase; with mmBase "entry" only a little below 1x), or whose price would be more than 1e9 times the entry. Check for null before doing arithmetic on it. When mmr plus liqFeeRate is at least 1/leverage the position is already at or below its maintenance margin at entry: liqPrice is the entry price and liquidatedAtEntry is true.

mmBase.description: Value the maintenance margin is taken on: "liquidation" = position value at the liquidation price (default; Bybit, KuCoin, Hyperliquid), "entry" = entry value (MEXC). Refused in tiered mode.

liqFeeRate.description: Liquidation fee as a fraction of position value, default 0, max 0.05; added to mmr (e.g. KuCoin 0.0006). Refused in tiered mode.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Deribit/Bybit/MEXC BTC-settled perps). Tiers and shared collateral: both (inverse: size in USD, bands and balances in the base coin).

size.description: Position size: base units for linear, USD contracts for inverse. Needed for tiered mode (tiers, walletBalance and the other fields select it); ignored otherwise.

tiers.description: Tiered mode (needs size): 1 to 50 maintenance margin tiers ascending by upTo (notional cap in quote for linear, in base coin for inverse, above 0; the last band is open-ended: an upTo given on the last tier is accepted and ignored); mmr 0 to 0.5 and not decreasing. cum = maintenance amount (Binance cum, Bybit mmDeduction); derived from the rates when omitted.

upTo.description: Notional cap of this tier (quote currency for linear, base coin for inverse); omit on the last tier.

mmr.description: Maintenance margin rate of this tier, as a fraction.

cum.description: Maintenance amount of this tier (Binance cum, Bybit mmDeduction; base coin for inverse); derived from the rates when omitted.

walletBalance.description: Shared collateral (needs size): wallet balance backing the position. Default: the isolated initial margin, size x entry / leverage in quote for linear, size / entry / leverage in the base coin for inverse.

otherMaintenanceMargin.description: Shared collateral (needs size): maintenance margin of other positions, 0 or more (default 0).

otherUnrealizedPnl.description: Shared collateral: unrealized PnL of other positions (default 0, may be negative).

tools.name: workflow.run_breakeven_planning
tools.title: Breakeven Planning
tools.description: Calculate the break-even exit price that covers all trading fees: this alone, nothing else. Edge cases: entryPrice and sizeBase above zero; feeOpenPct and feeClosePct fractions from 0 to 0.05 (defaults 0.0002 and 0.0005). Fees only. Not covered: funding (use workflow.run_funding_breakeven), slippage and spread. Use when user asks only "what price do I need to just break even?" and nothing more. If the user also gave a stop/target or wants a full trade-safety check, use workflow.run_risk_reward or workflow.run_pre_trade_check instead; both already include this breakeven figure plus more. Returns: breakevenPrice, totalFees.

sizeBase.description: Position size: base asset qty for linear, USD contracts for inverse

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, totalFees is returned in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_position_sizing
tools.title: Position Sizing
tools.description: Calculate the correct position size given a maximum risk in USDT and a stop-loss price. Edge cases: entryPrice, stopLoss and riskUsdt above zero; leverage above zero (default 1); fees 0 to 0.05; a fee and price combination that makes the risk denominator zero or negative is an error. Not covered: slippage past the stop, funding, exchange lot size and step rounding, and whether the margin is available. Use when user asks "how many coins should I buy?" or "size my position so I risk exactly $X". Returns: positionSize (base), positionUsdt, marginRequired.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, sizeQuote is USD contracts and margin is returned in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_funding_cost
tools.title: Funding Cost
tools.description: Calculate the total funding cost (or income) for holding a perpetual futures position. Edge cases: sizeBase, entryPrice and days above zero; fundingRate a fraction per interval (0.0001 is 0.01%), either sign; intervalHours 0.25 to 24 (default 8); if funding exceeds the position notional there is no finite price shift that offsets it, which is an error. Not covered: a funding rate that changes during the hold, and price moves. Use when user asks "how much funding will I pay holding X days?" or "is funding eating my profit?". Returns: totalCost (positive = you pay, negative = you receive; in the coin for inverse), costPerDay, annualPct, totalPeriods, breakevenShift (size of the price move whose PnL equals the funding: up for a positive rate, down for a negative one, for either side).

fundingRate.description: Funding rate per funding interval as a fraction, e.g. 0.0001 (per 8h unless intervalHours says otherwise)

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, which is the period fundingRate covers. Default 8 (3 payments a day); 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack, 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, sizeBase is USD contracts and cost figures come out in the base coin.

tools.name: primitive.average_entry
tools.title: Average Entry Price
tools.description: Calculate the weighted average entry price from multiple buy/sell fills (DCA): the bare number only, no breakeven or per-fill breakdown. Edge cases: symbol non-empty; at least one fill, each price and quantity above zero (size is accepted as quantity); leverage above zero is optional. The average is weighted by quantity. Not covered: fees, sells or partial closes (give only the fills still open), and funding. Use when user asks only "what's my average entry?" and wants just that figure. Each fill is { price, quantity } here (workflow.run_dca_entry calls the same field size). For breakeven and a per-level summary too, use workflow.run_dca_entry instead. Returns: averagePrice, totalSize, totalCost.

fills.description: Buy/sell fills to average, each with a price and a quantity (at least 1)

quantity.description: Fill quantity, required unless "size" is given (the same field)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined, average is the arithmetic mean (default). inverse = coin-margined, average is the harmonic mean (fill quantity is USD notional).

tools.name: workflow.run_exit_target
tools.title: Exit Target
tools.description: Calculate the exact exit price needed to hit a target PnL or ROE percentage. Edge cases: entryPrice, leverage and sizeBase above zero; targetMode pnl or roe, targetValue any number; fees 0 to 0.05 (defaults 0.0002 and 0.0005); a target that cannot be reached from this position is an error. Not covered: funding, slippage, liquidation before the target, and the chance that price gets there. Use when user asks "at what price do I take profit to make $500?" or "where should I set TP for 20% ROE?". Returns: targetExitPrice.

targetValue.description: Target value (USDT/coin for pnl mode, or %)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, pnl-mode targetValue and outputs are in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_scenario_planning
tools.title: Scenario Planning
tools.description: Run a scenario analysis: compute PnL for multiple price-change percentages at once. Edge cases: entryPrice and size above zero; at least one price change in percent; a change of -100 or less is refused for inverse contracts and exactly -100 is allowed for linear only; fees optional (default 0). Not covered: funding, liquidation along the path, slippage, and the probability of each scenario. Use when user asks "show me my P&L if BTC moves -10%, -5%, +5%, +10%". Returns: array of { deltaPct, exitPrice, netPnl, roe }.

deltasPct.description: List of price change percentages, e.g. [-10, -5, 0, 5, 10]. Must be at least -100 (exactly -100 only for linear contracts; inverse contracts need more than -100)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, size is USD contracts and pnl/fees come out in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_max_leverage
tools.title: Max Leverage
tools.description: Calculate the maximum leverage that keeps a position within a drawdown limit, from account size, max acceptable drawdown, and asset daily volatility. Edge cases: accountSize and volatilityPct above zero; maxDrawdownPct above 0 and at most 100; mmr 0 to 0.1 (default 0.005). A planning figure from the numbers you give, not a limit set by an exchange. Not covered: gaps and fat-tail moves beyond the volatility you state, exchange maximum leverage and tiers, funding, and fees. Use when user asks "what leverage does a 10% drawdown limit allow on BTC?" or "what leverage fits a 3% daily volatility and a 10% drawdown limit?". Returns: maxLeverage (maxDrawdownPct / (volatilityPct + mmr x 100), rounded down to 0.1, never below 1x), marginAtRisk (accountSize x maxDrawdownPct / 100, in USDT), safeMargin (USDT) and liquidationBuffer (percent). maxDrawdownPct and volatilityPct are percents (10 means 10%); mmr is a fraction (0.005 is 0.5%).

maxDrawdownPct.description: Maximum acceptable drawdown as percentage, e.g. 10 for 10%

volatilityPct.description: Expected daily price volatility as percentage, e.g. 3 for 3%

tools.name: primitive.hedge_ratio
tools.title: Hedge Ratio
tools.description: Calculate the short perpetual futures position size needed to hedge a spot holding. Default USDT-linear: sizes and costs in USD. With contractType "inverse" (coin-margined, needs entryPrice) the short is the same USD contracts and margin and funding come back in the base coin. Edge cases: spotSize above zero (USD value); hedgeRatio 0 to 200 percent (default 100); leverage 1 or more (default 1); fundingRatePct in percent per interval (0.01 is 0.01%, default 0.01); intervalHours 0.25 to 24 (default 8); an inverse contract needs entryPrice. Not covered: basis risk between spot and the perp, rebalancing as prices move, margin calls, and a funding rate that changes. Use when user asks "how much should I short to hedge my BTC?" or "what margin do I need for a 100% hedge?". Returns: perpNotional, requiredMargin, dailyFundingCost, annualFundingCost, hedgeCoverage, contractType and costUnit ("USD", or "base_coin" for inverse: read it before showing margin or funding as dollars). Inverse converts at the one entryPrice you give, so the coin figures assume the price stays there.

hedgeRatio.description: Percentage of spot to hedge, e.g. 100 for full hedge, 50 for half. Default 100.

leverage.description: Leverage on the perp short. Default 1.

fundingRatePct.description: Current funding rate per funding interval as a percentage, e.g. 0.01 (per 8h unless intervalHours says otherwise). Used for cost estimate.

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, the period fundingRatePct covers. Default 8 (3 payments a day); 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates); 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default). inverse = coin-margined: spotSize stays the USD value of the holding, requiredMargin and the funding costs are returned in the base coin.

entryPrice.description: Coin price in USD. Required for contractType inverse (converts the USD margin and funding to coin); ignored for linear.

tools.name: workflow.run_funding_arbitrage
tools.title: Funding Arbitrage
tools.description: Calculate funding rate arbitrage profit: annualized yield, net profit, and breakeven days for a long/short basis trade across two exchanges: the bare numbers only, no plain-English verdict. For the same math plus a profitable/marginal/loss verdict, use workflow.run_carry_trade instead. Edge cases: positionSize and durationDays above zero; longFundingRate and shortFundingRate in percent per interval (0.01 is 0.01%), either sign; transferFeePct 0 or more (default 0.1); intervalHours 0.25 to 24 (default 8). Not covered: price divergence between the venues, liquidation of either leg, margin on both venues, a rate that changes during the hold, and trading fees. Use when user asks "is this funding arb worth it?" or "how many days to break even on transfer fees?". Returns: netProfitUsdt, annualizedYieldPct, breakevenDays.

longFundingRate.description: Funding rate on long side (% per interval, positive = you pay)

shortFundingRate.description: Funding rate on short side (% per interval, positive = you receive)

transferFeePct.description: One-time transfer/setup fee as percentage, e.g. 0.1 for 0.1%

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, one interval for both legs. Default 8; 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates); 4 or 2 on some symbols. A leg paid on another interval is entered as its rate times (this interval / its own interval).

tools.name: workflow.run_compound_funding
tools.title: Compound Funding
tools.description: Project capital growth from reinvesting perpetual futures funding income (compounding carry). Edge cases: initialCapital above zero; fundingRatePct in percent per interval (0.01 is 0.01%), either sign; intervalHours a whole number that divides 24 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24, default 8); durationDays above zero and at most 3650; reinvestPct 0 to 100 (default 100); a result too large to represent is an error. Assumes the rate stays constant. Not covered: a changing rate, fees, taxes, and the capital limits a venue may set. Use when user asks "how much will I make compounding 0.01% funding for 90 days?" or "what's my APY on this carry position?". Funding received is split by reinvestPct (the rest is withdrawn and still counts as earned); funding paid comes out of capital in full, and the capital never goes below 0. Returns: finalCapital, totalWithdrawn, endValue, totalEarned, totalEarnedPct, annualizedAPY, dailyEarnings, snapshots.

fundingRatePct.description: Funding rate per interval as percentage, e.g. 0.01 for 0.01%

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, the period fundingRatePct covers, a whole number of hours that divides 24. Default 8; 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates); 4 or 2 on some symbols.

durationDays.description: Number of days to project, up to 3650

reinvestPct.description: Percentage of funding received that is reinvested each interval, 0-100 (the rest is withdrawn and counts as earned; funding paid always comes out of capital). 100 = full compounding. Default 100.

tools.name: workflow.run_pre_trade_check
tools.title: Pre Trade Check
tools.description: Full pre-trade decision card: orchestrates position sizing, breakeven, liquidation, and funding cost in one call. Edge cases: entry_price, leverage above zero; account_balance 0 or more; give desired_size, or stop_loss together with risk_pct, otherwise an error; funding_rate is a decimal per interval (0.0001 is 0.01%) and is read live from the exchange when omitted and exchange (and symbol) are given; hold_hours above zero (default 8); fees 0 to 0.05; mmr 0 to 0.2. Not covered: slippage, tiered margin (use workflow.run_liquidation_live), a funding rate that changes during the hold, and anything about where price will go; the verdict covers setup safety only. Use when user describes a full trade setup and asks "should I take this trade?" or "run the numbers on this setup". Provide exchange+symbol to fetch live funding rate automatically. For an R:R-graded verdict on an entry, stop and target, see workflow.run_risk_reward. Returns: positionSize, breakeven, liquidationPrice, fundingCost, overnightBreakevenShift, verdict. liquidation_price and the liquidation distance are null when the position cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less): check for null before using them.

exchange.description: Exchange code, e.g. "binance" or "bybit". Used to fetch the live funding rate if funding_rate is omitted, and to set funding_interval_hours when that is omitted (1 for Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack, whose rates are per hour; pass funding_interval_hours: 8 if you supply a rate that is per 8 hours). With funding_rate omitted and fetched live, funding_interval_hours is ignored and the interval the exchange reports for the symbol is used.

funding_rate.description: Funding rate per funding interval as decimal, e.g. 0.0001. If omitted, fetched live from exchange.

funding_interval_hours.description: Hours per funding payment, the period funding_rate covers: 8 on most venues, 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack, 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex. When funding_rate is omitted and fetched live (exchange and symbol given), any value passed here is ignored: the interval of that symbol as the exchange reports it is used (else the exchange default). Omitted otherwise: when you pass funding_rate yourself, the exchange default (1 for hourly venues, else 8), so pass funding_interval_hours for a symbol that pays every 4 or 2 hours.

hold_hours.description: Expected hold time in hours for overnight shift calc. Default 8.

mmBase.description: Value the maintenance margin is taken on: "liquidation" = position value at the liquidation price (default), "entry" = entry value.

liqFeeRate.description: Liquidation fee as a fraction of position value, default 0, max 0.05; added to mmr.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Bybit BTCUSD). All returned figures (notional, margin, risk_amount, funding_cost_*) stay USD-denominated either way; recommended_size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse.

tools.name: workflow.run_risk_reward
tools.title: Risk Reward
tools.description: Full risk:reward analysis: takes a trade with entry, stop, AND target (all three). Calculates R:R ratio, position size, liquidation price, breakeven, and P&L at both stop and target. Returns a verdict label, strong (3:1+) / good (2:1+) / marginal / poor, which grades the R:R ratio against fixed thresholds and is not a recommendation. For a full setup check tied to a live exchange/symbol (including funding cost), see workflow.run_pre_trade_check; its verdict covers overall setup safety, not just R:R. Edge cases: entry_price, stop_loss, take_profit, account_balance and leverage above zero; risk_pct above 0 and at most 100; fee_open_pct and fee_close_pct are fractions from 0 to 0.05 (defaults 0.0002 and 0.0005); mmr 0 to 0.2 as a fraction (0.005 is 0.5%); liqFeeRate 0 to 0.05. Stop and target distances are taken as absolute values from the entry, so a stop or target on the wrong side for the chosen side is not rejected: check the side yourself. Not covered: funding payments, slippage, partial fills, exchange tiered margin (use workflow.run_liquidation_live) and any guarantee that a stop fills at its price. Use when user asks "what's my risk reward on this setup?" or "what R:R do this entry, stop and target give?". liquidation_price and the liquidation distance are null when the position cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less): check for null before using them.

mmr.description: Maintenance margin rate as a fraction, 0 to 0.2 (default 0.005 = 0.5%); not a percent: 0.5% is 0.005, not 0.5

mmBase.description: Value the maintenance margin is taken on: "liquidation" = position value at the liquidation price (default), "entry" = entry value.

liqFeeRate.description: Liquidation fee as a fraction of position value, default 0, max 0.05; added to mmr.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Bybit BTCUSD). position_size/notional are USD notional (contracts) for inverse; pnl_at_stop/pnl_at_target come back denominated in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_portfolio_risk
tools.title: Portfolio Risk
tools.description: Aggregates risk across multiple open positions in one call: total notional, total P&L, total margin in use, margin usage as a % of account balance (if given), and which single position sits closest to liquidation. Each position is computed through the same canonical PnL/liquidation math as the single-position tools, then rolled up. Linear (USDT-margined) positions sum into one USD total; inverse (coin-margined) positions are grouped by settlement coin instead, since a BTC-margined P&L cannot be summed with an ETH-margined one without a live conversion rate. Returns a verdict label, healthy / watch / reduce / critical, which places the closest liquidation distance and margin usage in fixed bands and is not a recommendation. Edge cases: 1 to 50 positions; each needs entry_price, mark_price, size and leverage above zero, mmr 0 to 0.2 and fees 0 to 0.05 as fractions; an inverse position must name its settlement coin; account_balance above zero is optional and without it margin usage is not computed. Positions are not netted against each other. Not covered: correlation between positions, collateral shared across positions, exchange tiered margin, funding, and price moves after the mark price you give. Use when user asks "how exposed am I across all my positions?" or "which of my positions is closest to liquidation?". Position size follows the product-wide convention: base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse. liquidation_price and liq_distance_pct of a position are null when it cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less); the closest liquidation skips it.

positions.description: Open positions to aggregate (1 to 50). Each: { side, entry_price, mark_price, size, leverage }, plus optional fees, mmr, mmBase, liqFeeRate, contractType, coin, label.

label.description: Optional label to identify this position in the response (defaults to "Position N")

size.description: Position size: base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse

mmr.description: Maintenance margin rate as a fraction, 0 to 0.2 (default 0.005 = 0.5%); not a percent: 0.5% is 0.005, not 0.5

mmBase.description: Value the maintenance margin is taken on: "liquidation" = position value at the liquidation price (default), "entry" = entry value.

liqFeeRate.description: Liquidation fee as a fraction of position value, default 0, max 0.05; added to mmr.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Bybit BTCUSD)

coin.description: Settlement coin, required when contractType is inverse (e.g. "BTC", "ETH")

account_balance.description: Optional account balance in USD, used to compute margin_usage_pct: linear margin plus every inverse position's own margin marked to market at its mark_price, all as one USD total

tools.name: workflow.run_dca_entry
tools.title: DCA Entry
tools.description: DCA entry planner: weighted average entry price, breakeven, and per-level contribution from multiple fill prices and sizes. Each fill is { price, size } here (primitive.average_entry calls the same field quantity). Compared with primitive.average_entry, this one adds output for the case where breakeven or the per-level breakdown is also wanted, not just the bare average. Edge cases: 2 to 20 fills (size also accepted as quantity), each price and size above zero; fee_open_pct and fee_close_pct are fractions from 0 to 0.05 (defaults 0.0002 and 0.0005); every fill is on the same side and the same contract type. Not covered: fills at different times with different fees, partial closes, funding paid while the position was open, and liquidation (use workflow.run_liquidation_safety). Use when user bought at several prices and asks "what's my average entry?" or "where is my DCA breakeven?". Returns: averageEntry, breakeven, per-level summary.

entries.description: Fills to average (2 to 20). Each: { price, size }, e.g. [{ "price": 60000, "size": 0.5 }, { "price": 58000, "size": 1 }]. Size is base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse.

size.description: Fill size, required unless "quantity" is given (the same field)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. Each fill's size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse; averageEntry is then the harmonic mean of fill prices, not the arithmetic mean.

tools.name: workflow.run_average_down
tools.title: Average Down
tools.description: Should-I-average-down check: for an already-open position, compares adding more at a worse price against the always-available alternative of buying the same final total size fresh at today's price. Returns the new blended average entry, liquidation price and breakeven (before vs. after), margin_added (the actual cash/margin required for the add at this leverage, not the full notional), and three risk figures at your stop-loss: existing_risk (what you already risk, before adding), pyramid_risk (what you'd risk after adding), and clean_entry_risk (what a fresh entry at add_price for the same total size would risk). risk_penalty_pct is how much MORE than that fresh-entry alternative you're risking - for any genuine average-down (add_price worse than existing_entry_price) pyramid_risk is provably always greater than clean_entry_risk. liquidation_before_stop is true when the new liquidation price sits at or beyond your own stop-loss, meaning the exchange would force-close the position before the stop-loss ever triggers. Edge cases: all prices, sizes, stop_loss and leverage above zero; fee_open_pct and fee_close_pct are fractions from 0 to 0.05 (defaults 0.0002 and 0.0005); mmr 0 to 0.2; for a long the stop must be below the add price and for a short above it, otherwise an error (a stop that price already reached means the position should be closed). The risk comparison is meaningful only when the add is at a worse price than the existing entry. Not covered: funding, slippage, a stop that gaps through, and whether the market will recover. Use when user asks "should I add to this losing position?" or "what does averaging down actually cost me here?". liquidation_price and the liquidation distance are null when the position cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less): check for null before using them.

existing_entry_price.description: Entry price of the position already held

existing_size.description: Size already held: base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse

add_price.description: Proposed price to add at - also treated as today's current price for the fresh-entry comparison

add_size.description: Additional size being considered, same unit convention as existing_size

stop_loss.description: Stop-loss price (must be below add_price for a long, above it for a short - the position should already be closed otherwise)

mmr.description: Maintenance margin rate as a fraction, 0 to 0.2 (default 0.005 = 0.5%); not a percent: 0.5% is 0.005, not 0.5

mmBase.description: Value the maintenance margin is taken on: "liquidation" = position value at the liquidation price (default), "entry" = entry value.

liqFeeRate.description: Liquidation fee as a fraction of position value, default 0, max 0.05; added to mmr.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. Risk figures come back denominated in the base coin for inverse.

tools.name: workflow.run_scale_out
tools.title: Scale Out
tools.description: Scale-out planner: P&L, ROI, and cumulative P&L for each partial exit level. Edge cases: entry_price and total_size above zero; 2 to 10 exits, each price above zero and pct above 0 and at most 100, the pct values summing to at most 100 (less than 100 leaves the rest open); fees are fractions from 0 to 0.05. Not covered: the remainder not sold, funding, slippage, and the chance that each level is reached. Use when user wants to take profit at multiple targets: "close 30% at $90k, 30% at $95k, 40% at $100k, what's my total P&L?". Returns: per-level pnl, weightedAvgExitPrice, totalRoi.

total_size.description: Total position size in base currency

exits.description: Partial exit levels (2 to 10). Each: { price, pct }, e.g. [{ "price": 90000, "pct": 30 }, { "price": 95000, "pct": 70 }]; the pct values must not sum to more than 100.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. total_size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse, and per-level pnl comes back denominated in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_carry_trade
tools.title: Carry Trade
tools.description: Delta-neutral carry trade (funding arbitrage) analysis, with a profitable/marginal/loss verdict on top of the same math primitive.funding_arb uses. Compared with primitive.funding_arb, this one adds output for the case where a plain-English verdict is wanted, not just the raw numbers. Edge cases: notional and hold_days above zero; funding_rate_long and funding_rate_short are in PERCENT per interval (0.01 means 0.01%), either sign; transfer_fee_pct 0 or more, one way (default 0.1); interval_hours 0.25 to 24 (default 8), one interval for both legs. Not covered: price divergence between the two venues, liquidation of either leg, margin needed on both venues, rates that change during the hold, and withdrawal limits; the result assumes the rates stay as given. Use when user asks "is this carry trade worth it?": long on exchange A, short on exchange B, collect the funding rate spread. Returns: netYieldPct, grossProfit, netProfit, breakevenDays, verdict (profitable/marginal/loss).

funding_rate_long.description: Funding rate on the long exchange per interval, in percent (0.01 means 0.01%, not 0.0001)

funding_rate_short.description: Funding rate on the short exchange per interval, in percent (0.01 means 0.01%, not 0.0001)

interval_hours.description: Hours between funding payments, one interval for both legs (default 8; 1 for hourly venues; 4 or 2 on some symbols). A leg paid on another interval is entered as its rate times (this interval / its own interval).

tools.name: workflow.run_funding_breakeven
tools.title: Funding Breakeven
tools.description: Price move needed to cover funding cost + fees over a holding period. Edge cases: entry_price, size and hold_hours above zero; funding_rate is a decimal per funding interval (0.0001 is 0.01%), either sign; funding_interval_hours 0.25 to 24 (default 8); fees are fractions from 0 to 0.05. If carry cost exceeds what any price move can offset, the call is an error. Not covered: a funding rate that changes during the hold, mark versus last price, and slippage. Use when user asks "how much does BTC need to move for me to profit after funding?" or "is funding killing my edge on this trade?". Returns: breakevenWithFunding, breakevenWithoutFunding, requiredMovePct.

funding_rate.description: Funding rate per funding interval (decimal, e.g. 0.0001)

funding_interval_hours.description: Hours per funding payment, the period funding_rate covers: 8 (default), 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates), 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse; notional/funding_cost/fee_total/total_carry_cost come back denominated in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_crypto_profit
tools.title: Crypto Profit
tools.description: Profit or loss on a spot crypto trade (coins bought and sold outright, no leverage, no funding) after both fees. Give exactly one of investment (total cash spent, buy fee included) or quantity (coins bought). Each fee is a fraction of that fill's trade value (0.001 = 0.1%): the buy fee is paid on top of the coins' cost, the sell fee comes out of the sale value. For a leveraged perpetual futures position see workflow.run_pnl_planning. Edge cases: buyPrice and sellPrice above zero; give exactly one of investment (above zero, buy fee included) or quantity (above zero); buyFeePct and sellFeePct are fractions from 0 to 0.05 (default 0); holdingDays optional, annualized return only from 30 days. Spot only. Not covered: taxes, withdrawal and network fees, slippage, price moves in the quote currency, and leveraged positions (use workflow.run_pnl_planning). Use when user asks "I bought BTC at $X, what is my profit if I sell at $Y?" or "what price do I need to sell at to break even after fees?". Returns: quantity, totalCost, proceeds, totalFees, profit, roiPct and priceChangePct (fractions), priceMultiple, breakevenSellPrice, annualizedReturnPct (a fraction, only when holdingDays is given and is at least 30, null otherwise: annualizing a shorter hold gives meaningless figures).

buyPrice.description: Price paid per coin, in the quote currency (e.g. 60000 for BTC in USD)

sellPrice.description: Price per coin at the sale, or the price to test, same currency

investment.description: Total cash spent on the buy, buy fee included (e.g. 1000). Give this or quantity, not both

quantity.description: Number of coins bought (e.g. 0.5). Give this or investment, not both

buyFeePct.description: Buy fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05 (0.001 = 0.1%). Default 0

sellFeePct.description: Sell fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05 (0.001 = 0.1%). Default 0

holdingDays.description: Optional: days the coins were held; 30 or more also returns the annualized return

tools.name: workflow.run_spot_dca
tools.title: Spot DCA
tools.description: Dollar-cost averaging on a spot coin: the same cash amount bought at each of a list of prices (no leverage, no funding). Returns the coins held, total invested, the average price paid (below the plain average of the prices, because equal cash buys more coins when the price is low), the average cost per coin with the buy fee in it, the break-even sell price and, when currentPrice is given, the value, profit and ROI of selling everything there after the sell fee. amountPerBuy is the cash that leaves the account for one buy, buy fee included. Each fee is a fraction of that fill's trade value (0.001 = 0.1%, at most 0.05). Prices may be in any currency; results are in the same one. The average price is the harmonic mean of the prices; break-even = averageCostPerCoin / (1 - sellFee). Edge cases: 1 to 1000 prices; every price and amountPerBuy must be above zero; a list of one buy is valid; a non-finite result (huge or tiny inputs) is an error; without currentPrice no profit, ROI or proceeds are returned. Not covered: taxes, FIFO/LIFO lots, slippage, withdrawal or network fees, currency conversion, leverage and funding. For buys of unequal size or with sells in between use workflow.run_average_buy_price; for DCA on a perpetual futures position use workflow.run_dca_entry. Use when user asks "I buy $100 of BTC every week at these prices, what is my average and where am I now?". Returns: buys, totalInvested, totalQuantity, averageBuyPrice, averageCostPerCoin, simpleAveragePrice, lowestPrice, highestPrice, totalBuyFees, breakevenSellPrice, and (with currentPrice) currentValue, sellFee, proceeds, profit, roiPct (a fraction).

prices.description: Price paid per coin at each buy, in order (1 to 1000 positive numbers, e.g. [60000, 52000, 48000])

amountPerBuy.description: Cash spent on each buy, buy fee included (e.g. 100)

buyFeePct.description: Buy fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05 (0.001 = 0.1%). Default 0

sellFeePct.description: Sell fee for the exit, as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05. Default 0

currentPrice.description: Optional: the price to value the whole position at, same currency as prices

tools.name: workflow.run_average_buy_price
tools.title: Average Buy Price
tools.description: Real entry price of a spot coin bought and sold in several trades: moving average cost, trades in the order they happened, each with its own fee (no leverage, no funding). The buy fee is part of the cost basis; a sale removes coins at the current average and never changes the average of what is left, only a later buy does; selling everything resets it. Selling more than is held at that point is an error naming the trade. Each fee is a fraction of that trade's value (0.001 = 0.1%, at most 0.05). Edge cases: 1 to 1000 trades; price and quantity above zero; a sale before any buy, or above the holding, is an error; a sale within 1e-12 of the largest holding since the position was last flat counts as selling everything (float noise) and leaves exactly zero, never a residual; when nothing is held the average, before-fee average and break-even are null and costBasis is 0; realizedProfit can be negative. Not covered: taxes, FIFO/LIFO lots (moving average cost only), slippage, withdrawal or network fees, currency conversion, leverage and funding. Prices may be in any currency; results are in the same one. sellFeePct is the fee expected when the remaining coins are sold, used for the break-even sell price. For equal cash buys at a list of prices use workflow.run_spot_dca; for the average entry of a perpetual futures position use primitive.average_entry. Use when user asks "I bought and sold this coin several times, what is my average buy price and break-even now?". Returns: remainingQuantity, averageBuyPrice (fees in) and averageBuyPriceBeforeFees (null when nothing is held), costBasis, totalBought, totalSold, totalInvested, totalSellProceeds, realizedProfit, totalFees, breakevenSellPrice (null when nothing is held).

trades.description: Trades in the order they happened (1 to 1000)

feePct.description: Fee of this trade as a fraction of its value, 0 to 0.05. Default 0

sellFeePct.description: Fee expected when the remaining coins are sold, 0 to 0.05, for the break-even sell price. Default 0

tools.name: workflow.run_target_sell_price
tools.title: Target Sell Price
tools.description: The sell price that makes a target ROI or a target profit on a spot trade after both fees: the inverse of workflow.run_crypto_profit. Give exactly one of targetRoiPct (a fraction, 0.25 = 25%, negative for a stop price, above -1) or targetProfit (money; needs investment or quantity). Fees are a fraction of each fill's value (0.001 = 0.1%): the buy fee on top of the coins' cost, the sell fee out of the sale value (each fee at most 0.05); prices may be in any currency and results are in the same one; investment is the total cash spent, buy fee included. sellPrice = buyPrice x (1 + buyFee) x (1 + ROI) / (1 - sellFee); a target ROI of 0 is the break-even price. Edge cases: giving both or neither of targetRoiPct and targetProfit is an error; giving both investment and quantity is an error; targetProfit without a size is an error; a target that loses the whole stake or more (ROI of -1 or lower, or cost plus target profit at or below zero) is an error; a negative target gives a stop price below break-even. Not covered: taxes, FIFO/LIFO lots, slippage, withdrawal or network fees, currency conversion, leverage and funding. A target ROI does not depend on the size; with investment or quantity the cost, proceeds, profit and fees are returned too. Use when user asks "at what price do I sell to make 20% after fees?" or "to net $500 on this position, where do I put my limit sell?". Returns: sellPrice, requiredRoiPct (a fraction), priceChangePct, priceMultiple, breakevenSellPrice, and with a size: quantity, totalCost, sellValue, sellFee, proceeds, profit, totalFees (null without one).

targetRoiPct.description: Target return as a fraction of the cost (0.25 = 25%), above -1. Give this or targetProfit, not both

targetProfit.description: Target profit in money after both fees (negative for a loss limit). Needs investment or quantity. Give this or targetRoiPct, not both

investment.description: Total cash spent on the buy, buy fee included. Give this or quantity, not both

quantity.description: Number of coins bought. Give this or investment, not both

buyFeePct.description: Buy fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05 (0.001 = 0.1%). Default 0

sellFeePct.description: Sell fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05. Default 0

tools.name: workflow.run_present_value
tools.title: Present Value
tools.description: Present value of a future lump sum, a level payment stream, or both: what money received later is worth today at a discount rate. annualRate is a fraction (0.05 = 5%) split into periodsPerYear equal periods the nominal way (rate per period = annualRate / periodsPerYear); years x periodsPerYear is the number of periods, which must be whole when a payment is given. Payments are level and arrive at the end of each period, or at the start with paymentTiming "begin" (annuity due). Money received is positive, money paid is negative. A bond priced at its coupon rate comes back at its face value. For a list of uneven cash flows use workflow.run_npv. Edge cases: annualRate from -1 to 100 as a fraction (0.05 is 5%) with the rate per period above -100%; years 0 to 1000; periodsPerYear a whole number 1 to 365 (default 1); paymentTiming end (default) or begin; when a payment is given, years times periodsPerYear must be a whole number. A result too large to represent is an error. Not covered: a rate that changes over time, uneven payments (use workflow.run_npv), growing payments, inflation, taxes and fees, and a discount rate that fits the risk (you choose it). Use when user asks "what is $10,000 in 5 years worth today at 6%?" or "what is a 20-year stream of $500 monthly payments worth today?". Returns: presentValue, pvOfFutureValue, pvOfPayments, discountFactor, ratePerPeriod, periods, totalPayments, effectiveAnnualRate.

annualRate.description: Annual discount rate as a fraction (0.06 = 6%); may be zero or negative, but the rate per period must stay above -100%

years.description: Length in years, 0 to 1000 (fractions allowed for a lump sum; with payments years x periodsPerYear must be a whole number)

periodsPerYear.description: Compounding and payment periods per year, 1 to 365. Default 1 (12 = monthly)

futureValue.description: Lump sum received at the end, in any currency. Default 0

paymentTiming.description: "end" (ordinary annuity, default) or "begin" (annuity due, each payment one period earlier)

tools.name: workflow.run_future_value
tools.title: Future Value
tools.description: Future value of a starting sum, regular contributions, or both, grown at a fixed rate: what savings or an investment reach after a number of years. annualRate is a fraction (0.07 = 7%) split into periodsPerYear equal periods the nominal way (rate per period = annualRate / periodsPerYear); years x periodsPerYear is the number of periods, which must be whole when a payment is given. Contributions are level and made at the end of each period, or at the start with paymentTiming "begin". A fixed assumed rate, not a forecast and not a market-return simulation (for a range of outcomes use workflow.run_monte_carlo). Edge cases: annualRate from -1 to 100 as a fraction (0.05 is 5%) with the rate per period above -100%; years 0 to 1000; periodsPerYear a whole number 1 to 365 (default 1); paymentTiming end (default) or begin; when a payment is given, years times periodsPerYear must be a whole number. A result too large to represent is an error. Not covered: a rate that changes over time, uneven or growing contributions, inflation, taxes and fees, and any guarantee that the rate is earned. Use when user asks "what will $10,000 plus $500 a month be worth in 30 years at 7%?" or "how much will I have after 10 years of saving?". Returns: futureValue, fvOfPresentValue, fvOfPayments, growthFactor, ratePerPeriod, periods, totalContributions, interestEarned, effectiveAnnualRate.

annualRate.description: Annual growth rate as a fraction (0.07 = 7%); may be zero or negative, but the rate per period must stay above -100%

years.description: Length in years, 0 to 1000 (fractions allowed for a lump sum; with payments years x periodsPerYear must be a whole number)

periodsPerYear.description: Compounding and contribution periods per year, 1 to 365. Default 1 (12 = monthly)

presentValue.description: Starting amount, in any currency. Default 0

tools.name: workflow.run_npv
tools.title: Npv
tools.description: Net present value of a list of cash flows at a discount rate per period. The first flow is at time 0 and is NOT discounted (the usual textbook NPV; a spreadsheet NPV() function discounts the first value one period, so its result is this one divided by 1 + rate). Money received is positive, money paid is negative. ratePerPeriod must match the spacing of the flows (a monthly rate for monthly flows). To find the rate that makes NPV zero use workflow.run_irr. Edge cases: ratePerPeriod strictly above -1 and at most 1e6, as a fraction per period (0.05 is 5%), not per year; 1 to 1000 cash flows, the first at time 0, all finite; money received is positive and money paid is negative. Not covered: flows at irregular dates (use equal periods), a rate that changes, taxes, inflation, and the choice of discount rate; a positive NPV is arithmetic, not a decision. Use when user asks "is this project worth doing at a 10% cost of capital?" or "what is the NPV of these cash flows?". Returns: npv, discountedFlows, pvOfInflows, pvOfOutflows, undiscountedSum, periods.

ratePerPeriod.description: Discount rate per period as a fraction (0.1 = 10% per period), above -100%, at most 1e6

cashFlows.description: Cash flow at time 0, 1, 2, ... (e.g. [-1000, 500, 500, 500]); use 0 for an empty period

tools.name: workflow.run_irr
tools.title: Irr
tools.description: Internal rate of return: the rate per period at which the NPV of a list of cash flows is zero (first flow at time 0). The flows need at least one outflow and one inflow. One sign change in the flows (all outflows first, then all inflows) gives exactly one answer, returned as irr with unique true. With several sign changes there can be several rates or none: every rate found is listed in irrs and irr is null even when only one rate was found (reason "unverified"), with reason "multiple_roots" or "none_found" otherwise, so do not quote one rate as the return. With one sign change the search reaches about 1e13 per period; beyond that reason is "none_found". The search covers rates from -99% to +9,900% per period on a 0.2% grid of ln(1 + rate); two roots closer than that, or a root where NPV only touches zero, can be missed. Give periodsPerYear to also get the annual effective rate. Edge cases: 2 to 1000 finite cash flows with at least one inflow and one outflow, equal periods, first flow at time 0; periodsPerYear a whole number 1 to 365, optional. The rate is per period. Several sign changes can give several rates or none, then irr is null (see reason). Not covered: flows at irregular dates (that is XIRR), reinvestment at a different rate (that is MIRR), and a rate outside -99% to +9,900% per period. Use when user asks "what is the IRR of these cash flows?" or "what return does this project earn?". Returns: irr, irrs, unique, signChanges, reason, annualEffectiveRate, periods.

cashFlows.description: Cash flow at time 0, 1, 2, ... with at least one negative and one positive value (e.g. [-1000, 300, 400, 500])

periodsPerYear.description: Optional: periods per year (12 for monthly flows), 1 to 365, to also return the annual effective rate

tools.name: workflow.run_cagr
tools.title: Cagr
tools.description: Compound annual growth rate between a beginning and an ending value over a number of years: the constant yearly rate that turns one into the other, (ending / beginning)^(1 / years) - 1. A smoothed average: it hides the path and the volatility in between, and it says nothing about future growth. Both values must be positive. Edge cases: beginningValue and endingValue above zero (a start or end of zero or below has no growth rate); years above zero and at most 1000, a fraction of a year is fine. Not covered: contributions or withdrawals in between (that is not CAGR), the path and volatility between the two dates, and any forecast; CAGR smooths a bumpy path into one rate. Use when user asks "what is the CAGR of my portfolio?" or "what yearly growth takes $10,000 to $25,000 in 8 years?". Returns: cagr, totalReturn, growthMultiple, logGrowthRate (all fractions; logGrowthRate is the continuously compounded rate).

endingValue.description: Value at the end (positive), same currency

years.description: Years between them, above 0 and at most 1000 (fractions allowed, e.g. 2.5)

tools.name: workflow.run_apy_apr_converter
tools.title: Apy Apr Converter
tools.description: Convert an APR (nominal yearly rate) to an APY (effective yearly rate) or back, for a compounding you choose. APY = (1 + APR / m)^m - 1 for m periods a year, e^APR - 1 when continuous. The same APY is a different APR at every compounding frequency, so the frequency is required: give periodsPerYear (365 daily, 12 monthly) or continuous true, not both. Rates are fractions (0.12 = 12%). It converts rate arithmetic only: it does not include fees, token price moves or the risk that a pool rate changes. Edge cases: rate a fraction from -periodsPerYear (APR) or above -1 (APY) up to 1000; give periodsPerYear (1 to 365) or continuous true, never both and never neither; the rate per period must stay above -100%; a continuous APR above 709 (70,900%) is an error. Not covered: fees, token price moves, a pool rate that changes, taxes, and compounding that is not regular. Use when user asks "what APR is an 8% APY compounded daily?" or "what is 12% APR monthly as an APY?". Returns: apr, apy, periodsPerYear, continuous, ratePerPeriod, apyMinusApr, byCompounding (the same APY as an APR at annual, semiannual, quarterly, monthly, weekly, daily and continuous compounding).

direction.description: apr_to_apy converts the given APR into an APY; apy_to_apr the reverse

rate.description: The rate you have, as a fraction per year (0.12 = 12%), up to 1000. An APY must be above -1; an APR must satisfy APR / periodsPerYear above -1

periodsPerYear.description: Compounding periods a year, 1 to 365 (12 monthly, 365 daily). Omit when continuous is true

continuous.description: True for continuous compounding; then omit periodsPerYear

tools.name: workflow.run_bond_price
tools.title: Bond Price
tools.description: Price of a plain fixed-rate bond on a coupon date, with Macaulay duration, modified duration, convexity and DV01. Price = sum of the coupons and the face value discounted at the yield per period (yield / frequency), clean price, no accrued interest, so years x frequency must be a whole number of coupon periods. The yield is the nominal yearly yield to maturity compounded frequency times a year (the bond-market convention). Durations are in years, convexity in years squared. DV01 is the price fall for one basis point of yield, a positive number, the slope at the current yield and not a repricing. It does not include credit risk, call features, taxes or the day-count of a real settlement date. Edge cases: faceValue above zero and at most 1e12 (default 1000); couponRate 0 to 1 as a fraction; yieldRate -1 to 100 with the rate per period above -100%; years above zero and at most 100; frequency a whole number 1 to 12 (default 2); years times frequency must be a whole number of coupon periods. Not covered: accrued interest and a settlement date between coupons, credit risk, call and put features, floating coupons, taxes, and the day-count convention. Use when user asks "what is a 5-year 5% coupon bond worth at a 6% yield?" or "what is the duration and DV01 of this bond?". Returns: price, pricePctOfFace, status (premium, par, discount), pvOfCoupons, pvOfFace, couponPerPeriod, periods, yieldPerPeriod, currentYield, macaulayDuration, modifiedDuration, convexity, dv01.

faceValue.description: Face (par) value repaid at maturity, above 0 (default 1000)

couponRate.description: Annual coupon rate as a fraction of face value (0.05 = 5%), 0 to 1; 0 is a zero-coupon bond

yieldRate.description: Nominal yearly yield to maturity as a fraction (0.06 = 6%), compounded frequency times a year; yield / frequency must be above -1

years.description: Years to maturity, above 0 and at most 100; years x frequency must be a whole number (5 years semiannual is 10 coupons)

frequency.description: Coupon payments a year, 1 to 12 (default 2: semiannual; 1 annual, 4 quarterly, 12 monthly)

tools.name: workflow.run_bonding_curve
tools.title: Bonding Curve
tools.description: Pump.fun-style bonding curve calculator: exact tokens received for a buy, price impact, and graduation progress. Pure constant-product math (Uniswap V2 style) using pump.fun's official virtual-reserve constants: no live lookup needed, works for any token still on the curve (not yet graduated to a real AMM pool). Edge cases: solRaisedSoFar from 0 up to the graduation amount (a graduated token is out of range); solToSpend above zero. Pure constant-product math with pump.fun virtual-reserve constants, no live lookup. Not covered: the pump.fun trading fee unless stated in the result, slippage from other buyers landing first, tokens that already graduated to a real pool, and other launchpads with a different curve. Use when user asks "how many tokens do I get buying X SOL on this curve?" or "will this buy graduate the token?". Returns: tokensOut, priceImpactPct, progressPctBefore/After, willGraduate, partialFill (true if the buy exceeds remaining curve capacity).

solRaisedSoFar.description: SOL already raised on the curve so far (0 for a brand-new token)

tools.name: workflow.run_impermanent_loss
tools.title: Impermanent Loss
tools.description: Impermanent loss for a liquidity-pool position: compares providing liquidity against simply holding the same tokens, at a manually-supplied entry and current price. Two modes: full_range (standard 50/50 constant-product pool, the textbook 2*sqrt(k)/(1+k)-1 closed form) or concentrated (a Uniswap-V3-style position confined to [lowerPrice, upperPrice] - IL is always worse than full_range for the same price move when the range is tight, and the position is fully single-asset, no longer earning fees, once price exits the range). impermanentLossPct is always <= 0 and is measured relative to the quote token (dimensionless, exact regardless of what the quote token is); the optional dollar figures additionally assume the quote token's own USD price stayed roughly stable (true for a stablecoin-quoted pool). Edge cases: entryPrice and currentPrice above zero; concentrated mode needs both lowerPrice and upperPrice with lowerPrice below entryPrice and entryPrice below upperPrice; depositValueUsd above zero and feesEarnedUsd 0 or more are optional, and dollar figures are null without a deposit. Not covered: price moves inside the period, rebalancing, gas, tax, and a quote token whose own USD price moves (dollar figures assume it is stable). Use when user asks "how much am I losing to impermanent loss?" or "is this LP position still worth it after fees?". Returns: impermanentLossPct, lpValueMultiplier, hodlValueMultiplier, inRange, lossUsd/netResultUsd (null unless depositValueUsd given).

entryPrice.description: Base token's price in quote-token terms when liquidity was deposited

tools.name: workflow.run_options_payoff
tools.title: Options Payoff
tools.description: Payoff, P&L, and breakeven price for a single-leg Deribit BTC/ETH option (long or short call/put) at a given scenario price at expiry. Deribit BTC/ETH options are coin-settled: premium, P&L, and the max profit/loss caps come back denominated in the base coin (BTC/ETH), not USD; a scenarioPnlUsd convenience field converts the coin P&L back to USD at the scenario price. Coin settlement means a long call's upside is capped (max profit = 1 − premium per unit, not unlimited) while a long put's upside is technically unbounded as price falls toward zero, the mirror image of a USD-settled option's payoff shape, not a bug. Edge cases: strike, premium, quantity and scenarioPrice above zero; a coin premium for a call must be below 1. Not covered: early exercise, margin, fees, Greeks, the probability of profit and the value before expiry; the result is the payoff at expiry at one scenario price. Use when user asks "what does my BTC call/put pay off at price X?" or "where's my breakeven on this option?". Returns: intrinsicPerUnitCoin, scenarioPnlCoin, scenarioPnlUsd, breakevenPrice, maxLossCoin/maxProfitCoin (null = unbounded), isProfitable. With exchange "binance" (USDT-settled, flat payoff, premiumUsdt instead of premiumCoin) it returns the USDT equivalents: intrinsicPerUnitUsdt, scenarioPnlUsdt, breakevenPrice (K + premium for a call, K - premium for a put), maxLossUsdt/maxProfitUsdt (null = unbounded: a long call's profit is unlimited, a long put's best case is K - premium); USDT is not converted to USD.

exchange.description: Venue whose settlement rules apply. "deribit" (default): BTC/ETH, coin-settled, premium in the base coin. "binance": BTC/ETH/XAU/XAG, USDT-settled, flat payoff max(0, S-K) per unit, premium in USDT (use the *Usdt premium fields); the result carries exchange and settlement fields.

scenarioPrice.description: Underlying price in USD to evaluate the payoff at

tools.name: workflow.run_black_scholes
tools.title: Black-Scholes Option Price and Greeks
tools.description: Theoretical European option price and Greeks (delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho) from Black-Scholes, given manual spot/strike/days-to-expiry/volatility/risk-free-rate inputs plus an optional continuous dividend yield for stocks and ETFs (the implied-volatility and option-chain tools do not take one): no live data fetch. The live variant is workflow.run_black_scholes_live, which applies when checking a real Deribit, Binance or Bybit instrument, since that variant also reports how far the instrument's actual quoted price sits from what this formula implies. Prices are USD-denominated (the universal convention); callPriceCoin/putPriceCoin additionally divide by spot to match Deribit's own coin-settled quoting convention. Assumptions: European exercise only, one flat volatility for the whole life (no smile or skew), constant rate and dividend yield, a year of 365 calendar days, theta per calendar day. Edge cases: spot, strike, daysToExpiry and volatilityPct must be above zero; riskFreeRatePct and dividendYieldPct must be between 0 and 100, so a negative rate is refused; a deep out-of-the-money option returns a price and Greeks of exactly 0, and a very low volatility or very short expiry gives a very large gamma and theta, not an error. Not covered: early exercise (use workflow.run_american_option), discrete dividends, negative rates, transaction costs, taxes, margin, and Greeks adjusted for coin-settled (inverse) options: Greeks are standard USD Black-Scholes Greeks. Use when user asks "what should this option be worth at X% IV?" or wants raw Greeks for a hypothetical. Returns: callPriceUsd/putPriceUsd, callPriceCoin/putPriceCoin, deltaCall/deltaPut, gamma, vegaPerPct (per 1 vol point), thetaCallPerDay/thetaPutPerDay, rhoCallPerPct/rhoPutPerPct (per 1 rate point).

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days until expiry (can be fractional)

volatilityPct.description: Annualized implied volatility in percentage points, e.g. 60 for 60%

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points. Default 0: standard crypto-options convention.

dividendYieldPct.description: Continuous dividend yield in percent per year (1.2 means 1.2%), for stock and ETF options. Default 0: crypto has none. Range 0 to 100.

tools.name: workflow.run_option_greeks
tools.title: Option Greeks
tools.description: First and second order Greeks of a European option from Black-Scholes-Merton, manual inputs only (no live data): everything workflow.run_black_scholes returns (price, delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho) plus the higher-order Greeks vanna, vomma (volga), charm, veta, speed, zomma and color, with an optional continuous dividend yield for stocks and ETFs. Edge cases: daysToExpiry 0.001 to 36500, volatilityPct 0.01 to 1000, spot and strike above zero, riskFreeRatePct and dividendYieldPct 0 to 100; inputs so extreme that a Greek is not a finite number (a strike far from the spot for the volatility and time) are an error, not a null. Not covered: early exercise (use workflow.run_american_option), discrete dividends, a volatility smile (one flat volatility), negative rates, Greeks of coin-settled options; Greeks are USD Black-Scholes Greeks. Use when the user asks how delta changes when volatility or time moves (vanna, charm), how vega changes (vomma, veta) or how gamma changes (speed, zomma, color), or for an "option greeks calculator". Units: vannaPerVolPct = change of delta per 1 volatility point; vommaPerVolPct = change of vegaPerPct per 1 volatility point; charmCallPerDay/charmPutPerDay = change of delta when one calendar day passes; vetaPerDay = change of vegaPerPct when one calendar day passes; speedPerUsd = change of gamma per 1 unit of spot; zommaPerVolPct = change of gamma per 1 volatility point; colorPerDay = change of gamma when one calendar day passes. Time Greeks are the change as time passes (the derivative with respect to time to expiry, sign flipped); one input moves, the others stay fixed. Vanna, vomma, veta, speed, zomma and color are the same for the call and the put; charm differs by the dividend term only. A calendar day is 1/365 year.

strike.description: Strike price, same units as spot

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days until expiry (can be fractional), 0.001 to 36500

volatilityPct.description: Annualized implied volatility in percentage points, e.g. 60 for 60%, 0.01 to 1000

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points, 0 to 100. Default 0.

dividendYieldPct.description: Continuous dividend yield in percent per year, 0 to 100. Default 0.

tools.name: workflow.run_straddle_strangle
tools.title: Straddle and Strangle
tools.description: Payoff, P&L, and both breakeven prices for a long or short straddle/strangle (a call + a put on the same Deribit BTC/ETH underlying, both legs the same direction) at a scenario price. A straddle is callStrike === putStrike; any callStrike > putStrike makes it a strangle, same formula either way. Coin-settled like workflow.run_options_payoff: a long position's max loss is the flat total premium paid (between the strikes, both legs worthless); max profit is technically unbounded, dominated by the put leg's payoff as price falls toward zero. Edge cases: callStrike must be at or above putStrike; strikes, premiums and quantity above zero; for the Deribit coin-settled form callPremiumCoin plus putPremiumCoin must be below 1. Not covered: early exercise, margin, fees, Greeks and probability of profit; the result is the payoff at expiry at the one scenario price. Use when user asks about a straddle or strangle, e.g. "what does a BTC straddle pay off if price barely moves?" or "where are my breakevens on this strangle?". Returns: combinedIntrinsicCoin, scenarioPnlCoin, scenarioPnlUsd, upperBreakevenPrice, lowerBreakevenPrice, maxLossCoin/maxProfitCoin (null = unbounded), isStraddle, isProfitable. With exchange "binance" (USDT-settled, flat payoff, callPremiumUsdt and putPremiumUsdt) it returns: totalPremiumUsdt, combinedIntrinsicUsdt, scenarioPnlUsdt, upperBreakevenPrice (call strike + total premium), lowerBreakevenPrice (put strike - total premium, null when that is not above zero), maxLossUsdt/maxProfitUsdt (null = unbounded: the long side's profit is unlimited, the short side's loss is unlimited); USDT is not converted to USD.

exchange.description: Venue whose settlement rules apply. "deribit" (default): BTC/ETH, coin-settled, premium in the base coin. "binance": BTC/ETH/XAU/XAG, USDT-settled, flat payoff max(0, S-K) per unit, premium in USDT (use the *Usdt premium fields); the result carries exchange and settlement fields.

putPremiumCoin.description: Deribit only. Put leg premium per contract, in the base coin

callPremiumUsdt.description: Binance only. Call leg premium per unit, in USDT

putPremiumUsdt.description: Binance only. Put leg premium per unit, in USDT

tools.name: workflow.run_covered_call_protective_put
tools.title: Covered Call and Protective Put
tools.description: Covered call (long the coin + short a call against it, for yield) or protective put (long the coin + long a put, for downside insurance) on a Deribit BTC/ETH position. Returns the standard annualized-yield metric (premium ÷ 1 coin, annualized by 365/daysToExpiry) up front: that number doesn't depend on any price scenario. Also returns the USD value of the combined position at a given scenario price: covered call caps upside at strike + premium×scenarioPrice (the premium's own coin-denominated value still scales with price, unlike a textbook USD-settled cap); protective put floors value at strike×(1−premium), which is the true minimum across every possible settlement price, not just an approximation. Edge cases: spotEntry, strike, daysToExpiry, quantity and scenarioPrice above zero; premiumCoin above zero and at most 0.999 (Deribit form). The annualized yield is simple, 365 / daysToExpiry, not compounded. Not covered: early assignment, margin, fees, taxes, dividends, rolling, and the P&L before expiry. Use when user asks "what annualized yield do I get selling covered calls on my BTC?" or "how much does insuring my BTC with a put cost me?". Returns: staticYieldPct, annualizedYieldPct, valueAtScenarioUsd, breakevenPrice (covered_call only), floorValueUsd (protective_put only), vsHoldingUsd (vs. just holding the coin). With exchange "binance" (USDT-settled, premiumUsdt) the yield is premium divided by spotEntry (one unit is not a fraction of a coin), annualized by 365/daysToExpiry, and it returns: staticYieldPct, annualizedYieldPct, valueAtScenarioUsdt (covered call = min(S, K) + premium per unit), breakevenPrice (covered_call: spotEntry - premium, null when the cap sits below the cost), capValuePerUnitUsdt (covered_call: strike + premium), floorValuePerUnitUsdt (protective_put: strike - premium), vsHoldingUsdt; USDT is not converted to USD.

exchange.description: Venue whose settlement rules apply. "deribit" (default): BTC/ETH, coin-settled, premium in the base coin. "binance": BTC/ETH/XAU/XAG, USDT-settled, flat payoff max(0, S-K) per unit, premium in USDT (use the *Usdt premium fields); the result carries exchange and settlement fields.

tools.name: workflow.run_spread_payoff
tools.title: Spread Payoff
tools.description: Payoff, breakeven(s), and max profit/loss for a Deribit BTC/ETH vertical spread (2 legs, same option type, opposite direction, e.g. a bull call spread) or an iron condor/butterfly (4 legs: 2 calls + 2 puts) at a scenario price. Coin-settled, and the max profit/loss are genuinely NOT the flat, textbook USD-settled values: because each leg's own payoff is divided by the settlement price, (1) a debit vertical spread's peak payoff occurs exactly at its short strike, not "anywhere beyond it" - and its profit is a finite WINDOW that closes again at a high enough price, decaying back toward a full loss of the premium paid, and (2) an iron condor/butterfly's max loss is genuinely UNBOUNDED toward price->0 (maxLossCoin: null) if it has a put wing, unlike the "capped at wing width" USD-settled result - only the call side is actually bounded. Edge cases: 2 to 4 legs; strikes and premiums above zero; quantity and scenarioPrice above zero; the leg combination must form a vertical spread, iron condor or iron butterfly, otherwise it is an error naming the problem. Not covered: early exercise, margin, fees, Greeks, legs on different expiries (calendar and diagonal spreads), the probability of profit and the value before expiry. Use when user asks about a bull/bear call/put spread, vertical spread, iron condor, or iron butterfly, e.g. "what's my max loss on this BTC call spread?" or "where do my iron condor breakevens sit?". Returns: structureType (vertical_spread/iron_condor/iron_butterfly, inferred from the legs given), netDebitCoin (negative = credit received), scenarioPayoffCoin, scenarioPnlCoin/Usd, breakevenPrices (0-3, ascending), maxLossCoin/maxProfitCoin (null = unbounded), isProfitable. With exchange "binance" (USDT-settled, flat payoff) the textbook shapes apply instead of the coin-settled ones above: an iron condor's max loss is bounded (wing width less the credit) and a debit spread keeps its full profit above the short strike; it returns: structureType, netDebitUsdt, scenarioPayoffUsdt, scenarioPnlUsdt, breakevenPrices (ascending), maxLossUsdt (the worst P&L, negative when a loss; null = unbounded) and maxProfitUsdt (null = unbounded), isProfitable; USDT is not converted to USD.

exchange.description: Venue whose settlement rules apply. "deribit" (default): BTC/ETH, coin-settled, premium in the base coin. "binance": BTC/ETH/XAU/XAG, USDT-settled, flat payoff max(0, S-K) per unit, premium in USDT (leg premiumUsdt); the result carries exchange and settlement fields.

currency.description: Underlying. Default BTC. XAU and XAG (gold, silver) only with exchange binance.

legs.description: Exactly 2 legs (same option type, opposite position - a vertical spread) or 4 legs (2 calls + 2 puts - an iron condor/butterfly). Each leg: { optionType: call|put, position: long|short, strike: number, premiumCoin: number } for Deribit, premiumUsdt instead of premiumCoin for Binance.

premiumUsdt.description: Binance only. Premium per unit, in USDT

scenarioPrice.description: Underlying price in USD to evaluate the payoff at

tools.name: workflow.run_implied_volatility
tools.title: Implied Volatility
tools.description: Solves for the volatility that makes Black-Scholes reproduce an observed option price (Newton-Raphson with a bisection fallback for cases where vega is too flat to converge, e.g. deep ITM/OTM or very short-dated). Checks the price against its no-arbitrage bounds first and refuses to solve (converged: false + error) rather than return a garbage number when the price is impossible for the given spot/strike/rate. Edge cases: spot, strike, daysToExpiry and targetPriceUsd above zero; riskFreeRatePct 0 to 100; the search range is 0.01 to 1000 volatility points; a price outside the no-arbitrage bounds returns converged false with an error, not a number. Not covered: American exercise (a stock option price may imply a different volatility), dividends, a volatility smile, bid-ask spreads (one price in), coin-settled prices (convert to USD first). Use when user asks "what IV does this option price imply?" or gives a market price and wants the volatility, not the reverse. Returns: impliedVolatilityPct, iterations, method (newton-raphson/bisection), converged, identifiable, warning, priceAtSolution. identifiable is false when many volatilities reproduce the price (deep ITM, far OTM): warning then says the returned volatility is one of them. When converged is false, identifiable is false and error explains.

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points. Default 0: standard crypto-options convention.

targetPriceUsd.description: The observed option price, USD, to solve the implied volatility from

tools.name: workflow.run_barrier_touch
tools.title: Barrier Touch
tools.description: Probability that the price touches a barrier (a target or a stop level) at ANY time within N days, under geometric Brownian motion (reflection principle with drift). This is not the probability of finishing beyond the level at expiry: at zero log-drift a touch is exactly twice as likely as a finish, and `finishBeyondProbabilityPct` is returned next to it for comparison (the end-of-window question itself is `workflow.run_window_fair_value`). Barrier above spot gives an up-touch, below spot a down-touch. Monitoring is continuous (every instant, not daily closes or candle highs, which touch less often); year is 365 days; `driftPct` is the annualized expected price drift, default 0. Output: touchProbabilityPct, finishBeyondProbabilityPct, direction, barrierDistancePct. Edge cases: spot, barrier and daysToExpiry (at most 3650) above zero; volatilityPct 0.01 to 1000; driftPct -1000 to 1000; barrier and spot must be within a factor of about 5e8 of each other. Not covered: a discrete-monitored barrier, knock-in or knock-out option prices, jumps, volatility that changes over time, trading costs; the probability is under a constant volatility and drift.

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days in the window (can be fractional, up to 3650)

volatilityPct.description: Annualized volatility in percentage points (e.g. 60 for 60%), at least 0.01
