tools.name: workflow.run_forex_correlation_live
tools.title: Forex Correlation (Live)
tools.description: Correlation coefficient and minimum-variance hedge ratio between two forex pairs, fetched live: historical daily rates for both pairs over the given lookback window (frankfurter.app's daily ECB reference time series, business days only), aligned by matching date, computed on daily % returns. hedgeRatio follows Hull's standard futures-hedging formula: "how many units of pair2 per unit of pair1 minimizes the combined position's variance." Edge cases: days is a whole number from 14 to 365 (default 30) of calendar days, so fewer trading days are used; both pairs must be BASE/QUOTE of two different ISO 4217 codes; dates present in only one series are dropped; too few overlapping dates, or a flat series, gives available false. Daily ECB reference rates only, no intraday data. Not covered: lagged correlation, rolling windows and significance tests. Use when user asks "how correlated are EUR/USD and GBP/USD?" or "what hedge ratio should I use between these two pairs?". Returns: n (overlapping trading days used), correlation (-1 to 1), hedgeRatio, available (false + error if either pair has no data, or too few dates overlap). If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

pair1.description: First currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

pair2.description: Second currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "GBP/USD"

days.description: Calendar days to look back, 14-365. Default 30. Business-day-only data means fewer actual points than this number.

tools.name: workflow.run_price_consensus
tools.title: Price Consensus
tools.description: Cross-exchange agreement check for one perpetual futures price: fetches the same asset USDT/USDC-margined perpetual from a reference set of 7 liquid exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, Hyperliquid, MEXC; the chosen one is compared against the rest) and reports the median of the others, the spread across all, and how far the chosen exchange sits from that median. Says the exchanges disagree instead of guessing: status is agree (under 0.25%), warn (0.25% to 1%), diverge (1% or more) or insufficient (fewer than 3 other exchanges returned a comparable contract; inverse, dated and unlisted contracts are not compared, and that is not a verdict on the price). Use before acting on a live price: "is this Bybit BTC price in line with the market?" Symbol is the perp symbol as that exchange names it (e.g. BTCUSDT on bybit, ETH-USDT-SWAP on okx). Returns: status, summary, median, peerMedian, spreadPct, deviationPct, sources, quotes (price per exchange), thresholds_pct, as_of. Edge cases: exchange must be a known code and symbol is that exchange own perp name (1 to 60 characters); fewer than 3 comparable peers, an unknown symbol, an inverse or dated contract or a failed quote gives status insufficient with a reason, never a guess. Not covered: order book depth, funding and basis differences between venues, spot prices, and any claim about which exchange is right; it checks agreement of last quotes only.

exchange.description: Exchange code of the price being checked, e.g. bybit, binance, okx, gate, kucoin, hyperliquid, mexc

symbol.description: That exchange's own perpetual symbol, e.g. BTCUSDT (bybit/binance), ETH-USDT-SWAP (okx), BTCUSDC (hyperliquid)

tools.name: workflow.run_prediction_market_edge
tools.title: Prediction Market Edge
tools.description: Compares your own probability estimate for an event against a prediction market's price (manual entry, or a live Kalshi ticker, Limitless slug, or Myriad slug) and sizes a bet using fractional Kelly criterion bet sizing (default: quarter-Kelly, a standard conservative haircut on full Kelly, stated explicitly as a convention). Returns a zero Kelly stake whenever your probability doesn't exceed the market's price: no edge. Edge cases: yourProbabilityPct 0.01 to 99.99; give exactly one of marketProbabilityPct (0.01 to 99.99) or a kalshiTicker, limitlessSlug or myriadSlug; bankrollUsd above zero; kellyFractionCap 0.01 to 1 (default quarter-Kelly); no edge (your probability not above the price) gives a zero stake. Not covered: how good your probability is (Kelly with a wrong estimate overbets), fees, slippage, correlated bets, and a limit on market depth. Use when user asks "does this bet have edge?" or "what does Kelly sizing give for my probability estimate against the market's price?". Provide exactly one of marketProbabilityPct/kalshiTicker/limitlessSlug/myriadSlug. Returns: edgePct, evPerDollarStaked, fullKellyFraction, cappedKellyFraction, recommendedStakeUsd, verdict (a label for the size of cappedKellyFraction: skip_this_one/think_twice/worth_the_risk/take_it, not a recommendation). If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

marketProbabilityPct.description: The market's probability (price), 0.01-99.99. Use this OR one of the live sources below, not both.

kalshiTicker.description: A Kalshi market ticker to fetch the market probability from live instead of supplying it manually.

limitlessSlug.description: A Limitless Exchange market slug to fetch the market probability from live instead of supplying it manually.

bankrollUsd.description: Bankroll available for this bet, in USD

kellyFractionCap.description: Fraction of full Kelly to actually stake, 0.01-1. Default 0.25 (quarter-Kelly).

tools.name: system.verify
tools.title: Verify Calculations
tools.description: Run the full regression suite: 60 canonical test vectors (linear and inverse/coin-margined) across all 12 calculators, and return a pass/fail report with counts and timestamp. Useful as a health check before relying on results in production workflows.

tools.name: system.pubkey
tools.title: Signing Public Key
tools.description: Return the ECDSA P-256 public key (PEM + JWK) and canonical signing format used to sign tool responses, so results can be verified offline without calling back to TradingCalc. Every tools/call result includes a signed second content block when signing is configured; also available at GET /api/mcp/pubkey.

tools.name: system.batch
tools.title: Batch
tools.description: Run up to 10 calls of other tools in one request and get all results back together, in order. Each entry is {name, arguments} exactly as for a single call; each result carries its own signature block, so every one verifies on its own. The batch call itself is free: every entry counts as one call against the daily limit. A failed entry does not stop the others (it comes back with an error), except that once the daily limit is reached or the batch has run for about 20 seconds, the entries after that point are not run and not counted: the reply says so for each, so send them again. A batch cannot contain a batch. Entries run one after another, in order, and none sees the output of another.

name.description: Tool name as listed by tools/list, for example workflow.run_var_cvar
